hypothesis: A public cold entry plus separately sealed private terminal entry can carry x3 length/x4 item-base/x5 positive handle between proved closed mode2 Vec functions, dynamically validating handle equality at every read/write and reducing repeated descriptor lookup beyond variation.
design: Start from qualified small-tail-frame source; exclude both rejected local candidates and unsigned-less implementation. No source-name/workload matching.
Only actual mode2 F0 with NP1 Vec, NS/DP<=3, no spills/outgoing/returning/unknown calls or allocations. Prove spare x3/x4/x5 across each allowed operation; restrict forms if not proved.

Public entry initializes key0; private entry may skip exactly that initialization only on a proved compatible closed direct terminal edge. Function addresses/exports/imports and unknown callees use public entry.

Prove target classification from exact typed SIR and original prescan, including actual slot/depth bounds, open metadata, own labels and a real unexpanded terminal call. Validate emitted private-entry marker during layout; seal generator/layout/internal ABI in artifact recipes.

Every vector access still dynamically compares the actual handle against a nonzero validated key; misses retain original handle then index checks and capture immutable descriptor. Hits retain actual writer/read index check. Allocation/metadata mutation/unknown effects/unsafe targets cannot carry descriptor.
Original five-word published fuel stays at every original charge, including inline wrappers. No precharge/speculative access, same trap and partially written items with fuel/resource exhaustion.

Do not infer descriptor validity from observed equal handles. Independent cold/public/private/changed/invalid/alias and all-op scratch controls, open/label/field/type/entry mutations, original508/14523, four native selfbuilds, all19 states/instructions, then unchanged-rule timing of every changed guest.
Permanent fixtures, normal gates, committed-source three-generation integrated rebuild and command/corpus/all19 measured-code parity required before adoption.
